chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever is killed defending his property/rights, he is a martyr."
Then he said, "O Abu Maryam, do you know what 'defending his property/rights' means?"
I said, "May I be your ransom, a man is killed defending his family and his wealth and similar things."
He said, "O Abu Maryam, indeed among the aspects of jurisprudence is knowing the truth."

key_terms.مَظْلِمَتِهِ: His property/rights (specifically wealth or family being defended)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a martyr who is killed defending their property in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq, the concept of martyrdom is expanded beyond battlefield death to include those killed defending their 'mazlamah' (property, family, or self), illustrating the practical application of legal definitions. The Imam’s concluding remark, 'Indeed, part of jurisprudence is knowing the truth,' emphasizes that true fiqh requires deep contextual understanding rather than mere literalism, a key tenet in Shia legal theory.
